Shri Mayank Upadhyay, Advocate for the respondent No.
 Company.
ORDER IA No.1150/2024 taken up, which is an application for condonation of delay.
The appeal is barred by 492 days.
For the reasons stated in the application, IA No.1150/2024 is allowed.
Delay of 492 days in filing the appeal is hereby condoned.
With the consent of parties, heard finally and decided separately.

The appellant/claimant has filed this appeal under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 being aggrieved by award dated 25.03.2023 passed in Claim Case No.174/2022 by the Member,
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District Ujjain (M.P.), whereby a total compensation amount of Rs.5,27,000/- has been awarded in favour of the claimant.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District Ujjain
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The present appeal is filed seeking enhancement in compensation amount upto Rs.2,00,000/-.
The date of accident and negligence are not in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:11936 2 MA-7089-2023 dispute in this case.

3. In short, the facts of the case are that on 22.06.2018, the appellant Ramsingh, aged 66 years was going on his motorcycle to his farmhouse, at the same time, the offending tractor bearing Ramsingh vs Ishwer Singh on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34909389/
1 registration No.MP13-AB-5326 driven by respondent No.1 very rashly and negligently dashed against the motorcycle of appellant, thereby the appellant has suffered crush injury of right leg below knee.
4. Learned Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the income and permanent disability suffered by the claimant, which is on lower side.

Learned Tribunal while awarding the amount of compensation has considered the entire evidence placed on record and after recording evidence Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.5,27,000/- under the following heads :-
 Head Amo

Permanent disability Rs.1,02 Medical expenses, diet, attendance, transportation Rs.4,20,000/-
 expenses  Pain & suffering Rs.5,000/-
Total Rs.5,27,00 5

. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case as the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
It is submitted that the Medical Board has assessed 50% permanent disability vide Ex.P/234 and the Doctor (PW-4) assessed 1/3 permanent disability

however, learned Tribunal has committed error in not considering the same and has only assessed 17% under permanent disability for the whole body, whereas the appellant has suffered crush injury of right leg below knee and was admitted in the hospital for 06 days.
Appellant has suffered three compound fracture of his NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:11936 3 MA-7089-2023 tibia and fibula bone and his ligament of his right shoulder was broken.
The Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding any sum under the head of future prospects.
The appellant was an agriculturist and milk vendor by profession.

Due to the accident, he has suffered several injuries in different parts of body,
which made him incapable for doing his physical work.
The compensation awarded on other heads by the learned Tribunal is also on very lower side.
The interest of 6% is also on very low as per settled law on this point.

Considering the permanent disability certificate, which is a case of crust injury below right knee, 30% permanent disability should be assessed whereas, the Tribunal has assessed 17% permanent disability to the claimant in this case.
The income of the appellant is calculated by the Tribunal as Rs.10,000/- per month with a multiplier of 5, which is also on the lower side.
Considering the year of accident i.e. 2018 and appellant being an agriculturist having 7.310 hectare agricultural land, his income should have been assessed as Rs.12,000/- per month.
It is also submitted that nothing was given under other heads.
On these grounds, it is prayed for enhancement of compensation.

6. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/Insurance company has opposed the submissions made by counsel for the appellant and submitted that the Tribunal has not committed any error and has rightly passed the award in favour of the appellant.
Hence, prayer for enhancement of compensation be rejected.

2 7 .

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the record, more particularly the age of the claimant, nature of injuries, in the considered opinion of this Court, it is revealed that proper amount has not been awarded to the claimant for permanent disability whereas, the Doctor Mahesh NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:11936 4 MA-7089-2023 Marmat (PW-4) has clearly opined 1/3 permanent disability.

Certainly, no opinion is adverted with regard to permanent disability of whole body, but looking to the injuries, it can be assumed that the injured has 30%
disability.
Since, the income of the injured is assumed as Rs.12,000/- per month thus, the compensation amount is recalculated.
Further, after multiplier of 5, should be applied 30% of permanent disability in annual income.

Likewise, awarded amount in other heads is also required to be enhanced as follows :-
 HEADS AMOUNT  Permanent Disability Rs.12000/- per month   =Rs.1,44,000/- X 5 (M  30% (P.D.)
 =Rs.2,16,000/-
 Loss of income/earning during Rs.30,000/- (for 2.5   treatment  Medical Expenses Rs.4,13,900/-
 Pain and suffering Rs.15,000/-

Transportation charges Rs.10,000/-
 Special diet Rs.10,000/-
Attendant expenses Rs.10,000/-

MACT Awarded Amount Rs.5,27,000/-
 Enhanced Amount Rs.1,77,900/-
8.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.7,04,900/- as against the Award of the Claims Tribunal of Rs.5,27,000/-.
Accordingly, the appellant/claimant is entitled to an additional sum of Rs.1,77,900/- over and above the amount, which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
9. In the result, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed, by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.1,77,900/-.

The enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by the learned Claims Tribunal from the date NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:11936 5 MA-7089-2023 of filing of claim petition till its realization.
The said amount be paid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Rest of conditions as imposed by learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

10. If the enhanced amount of compensation is in excess to the valuation of appeal, the difference of the Court fee (if not already paid) shall be deposited by the appellant- claimant within a period of one month and proof thereof, shall be submitted before the Registry.
Thereafter, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of the order passed today.
11. In view of above, miscellaneous appeal filed by the appellant/claimant stands disposed of.
